blindSummary:
This state/province diverges from the union-wide baseline in one live, visitor-relevant direction: a 2021 hate-crime and public-order statute (in force 1 April 2024) created the union's only dedicated transgender-identity hate-crime charging aggravation. The prosecution service reported 104 charges carrying that aggravation in 2025-26 (up 21% on 86 the year before), and the police recorded 8,538 hate crimes in 2024-25 - the first full year of the statute. Anti-trans offending is therefore named in charging here as a distinct statutory category; in the union's other main jurisdictions, transgender identity appears in police recording as one of five monitored strands, but no equivalent transgender charging aggravation exists. For an assaulted or harassed visitor that is the difference between a crime the prosecution system is built to identify by name and one it is not. The wider climate corroborates the law: the devolved legislature passed expansive gender-recognition reform by a two-thirds majority, and public opinion here on LGBT equality runs consistently ahead of the union-wide average.

What does not count as local hostility: the order blocking that reform and the June 2026 senior-court ruling voiding the prison service's trans custody guidance were both applications of union-wide law and the union supreme court's biological-sex definition - the same mechanisms visitors face in every jurisdiction of the union. They erased this state/province's attempt to rise above that baseline; they did not push it below. The charging machinery, plus the most trans-accepting electorate and government in the archipelago, are the local facts.

Direct evidence that the dedicated transgender aggravation under the 2021 statute is actively used in charging decisions.

Official police statistics on hate crimes recorded in this jurisdiction for 2024-25 - the first annual report under the 2021 statute's reporting provision: 8,538 recorded hate crimes with breakdowns of type, victim/perpetrator characteristics and prejudice shown.

An interior-ministry statistical release on police-recorded hate crime in the union's other main jurisdictions, year ending March 2025: 115,990 offences across five monitored strands, with the transgender strand down 11% on the year. Establishes the comparison baseline: those jurisdictions monitor transgender identity in recording but have no statutory transgender charging aggravation, unlike this jurisdiction's 2021 statute.
